{{Short description|French physicist (born 1948)}}
'''Dominique Franck Escande''' (born 1948) is a French physicist. He is known for his research in foundations and methods of plasma physics,<ref>{{Citation |last=Escande |first=Dominique F. |chapter=How to Face the Complexity of Plasmas? |date=2013 |title=Nonlinear Systems and Complexity |pages=109–157 |chapter-url=https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4614-6962-9_4 |access-date=2026-02-07 |place=New York, NY |publisher=Springer New York |isbn=978-1-4614-6961-2}}</ref> wave-particle interactions in plasmas, Hamiltonian dynamics, deterministic chaos, thermonuclear fusion by magnetic confinement, self-organization of the reversed field pinch, plasma-wall self-organization in magnetic fusion<ref name=orcid>Dominique Franck Escande {{ORCID|0000-0002-0460-8385}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Citation |last=Elskens |first=Yves |chapter=Hamiltonian chaos |date=2019-09-17 |title=Microscopic Dynamics of Plasmas and Chaos |pages=94–140 |chapter-url=https://doi.org/10.1201/9780429139987-5 |access-date=2026-02-07 |publisher=CRC Press |isbn=978-0-429-13998-7 |last2=Escande |first2=Dominique}}</ref>

==Education and career==
After graduating in physics in 1967 from the [[École polytechnique]], Dominique Franck Escande became a graduate student in physics at [[Paris-Sud University]]. There he graduated in 1971 with a {{ill|diplôme d'études approfondies|fr}} (DEA) and a Ph.D. in 1978.<ref name=orcid/> His Ph.D. thesis is entitled ''Ondes haute fréquence dans un plasma en présence de fluctuation de basse fréquence'' (High-frequency waves in a plasma in the presence of low-frequency fluctuation).<ref name=MathGen>{{MathGenealogy|id=108342|name=Dominique Franck Escande}}</ref> From 1981 to 1992 he was a [[CNRS]] researcher at the École polytechnique, where he held an appointment as [[Academic ranks in France|''maître de conférences'' (assistant professor)]] in physics. During the years of his appointment at the École polytechnique, he also worked at several other scientific institutions. For the academic year 1983–1984 he was on sabbatical at the [[University of Texas at Austin]]'s Institute for Fusion Studies (IFS)<ref name=orcid/> (which, among other things, was the principal site for USA-Japan collaboration on theory in fusion research).<ref>{{cite web|title=Theory Group, Institute for Fusion Studies|website=University of Texas at Austin|url=https://w3fusion.ph.utexas.edu/ifs/}}</ref> From 1987 to 1992 he was a part-time consultant for X-Recherche Service.<ref name=orcid/> In 1988 he created, in collaboration with Fabrice Doveil, the research team Equipe Turbulence Plasma inside laboratory Physique des Intéractions Ioniques et Moléculaires (PIIM) at Université de Provence in Marseille.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Elskens |first=Y. |last2=Escande |first2=D. |date=April 2003 |title=BOOK REVIEW: Microscopic Dynamics of Plasmas and Chaos |url=https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2003PPCF...45..521E/abstract |journal=Plasma Physics and Controlled Fusion |language=en |volume=45 |issue=4 |page=521 |doi=10.1088/0741-3335/45/4/701 |issn=0741-3335}}</ref> From 1988 to 1992 Escande held an appointment as CNRS researcher in this laboratory.<ref name=orcid/>

Escande was from 1992 to 1996 the head of the ''Département de Recherches sur la Fusion Contrôlée'' at [[Cadarche|CEA-Cadarache]], [[WEST (formerly Tore Supra)|whose activity was centered on the Tore Supra tokamak group]]. From 1995 to 1996 he chaired the [[Euratom]] Fusion Technology Steering Committee-Implementation. At ''{{ill|Consorzio RFX|it}}'' (Consortium RFX) in [[Padua]], Italy, he was from 1996 to 1998 a full-time advisor and is since 1998 a part-time advisor. In 1998 he became a CNRS researcher at the laboratory PIIM, where he now has emeritus status as Directeur de Recherche Emérite.<ref name=orcid/>

He contributed three book chapters.<ref name=orcid/><ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last=Liu |first=Jiaxing |last2=Zhu |first2=Ping |last3=Escande |first3=Dominique Franck |last4=Liu |first4=Wenbin |last5=Xue |first5=Shiwei |last6=Lin |first6=Xin |last7=Tang |first7=Panjun |last8=Wang |first8=Liang |last9=Yan |first9=Ning |last10=Yang |first10=Jinju |last11=Duan |first11=Yanmin |last12=Jia |first12=Kai |last13=Wu |first13=Zhenwei |last14=Cheng |first14=Yunxin |last15=Zhang |first15=Ling |date=January 2026 |title=Accessing the density-free regime with ECRH-assisted ohmic start-up on EAST |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/sciadv.adz3040 |journal=Science Advances |volume=12 |issue=1 |article-number=eadz3040 |doi=10.1126/sciadv.adz3040 |pmc=12757026 |pmid=41477826}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=EAST Tokamak experiments exceed plasma density limit, offering new approach to fusion ignition |url=https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/1111089 |access-date=2026-02-07 |website=EurekAlert! |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite journal |last=Basu |first=Mohana |date=2026-01-09 |title=Chinese nuclear fusion reactor pushes plasma past crucial limit: what happens next |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-00063-4 |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=649 |issue=8097 |pages=534–535 |doi=10.1038/d41586-026-00063-4 |issn=1476-4687|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He is the co-author with Yves Elskens (a physics professor at the University of Provence) of the book ''Microscopic dynamics of plasmas and chaos'' (2003, [[IOP Publishing]]); with a 2019 paperback edition published by [[CRC Press]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

His former doctoral student Didier Bénisti<ref name="MathGen" /> has acquired an international reputation in fusion research and plasma physics.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Invited Speakers|website=53rd Annual Meeting of the APS Division of Plasma Physics, November 14–18, 2011; Salt Lake City, Utah; American Physical Society|volume=56 |issue=16 |url=https://meetings.aps.org/Meeting/DPP11/APS_Invited}}</ref>

In 1994 Escande was awarded the [[Prix Paul Langevin]].
